description_short.value: Kumasi-based brewer and drinks distributor making Guinness and other beers and malts under licence, and selling international spirits; majority-owned by the Castel Group since July 2025.
description_short.source: Written by us from the Guinness Ghana Breweries PLC 2025 Annual Report (GSE PR 375/2025: report of the directors, nature of business; chairman's statement; note 32, subsequent events)

description_full.value: Guinness Ghana Breweries PLC makes, distributes and sells alcoholic and non-alcoholic drinks. It brews at two breweries, at Kaase in Kumasi, where its registered office is, and at Achimota in Accra. It was first registered in 1960 and has been listed on the Ghana Stock Exchange since 23 August 1991. For most of its listed life it was a subsidiary of Diageo. On 3 July 2025 Diageo sold its 80.4% stake to Boissons Nouvelles Holding, part of the French-owned Castel Group, at GHS 5.15 per share. Diageo kept the Guinness brand: the company still brews Guinness and other Diageo brands under long-term licences, and distributes Diageo's international spirits, such as Johnnie Walker and Baileys, under a separate agreement. Before the sale, SSNIT was the second-largest shareholder, with 7.57% at 30 June 2025. Revenue for the year to 30 June 2025 was GHS 3.6 billion. To match Castel's calendar year, the company has moved its year end from 30 June to 31 December: the current financial period runs from 1 July 2025 to 31 December 2026, and audited accounts for it are due by the end of March 2027. It reports in Ghana cedis.
